source_excerpt:
▶ Browse all 150 shots in the Gallery · 🎬 Watch the Showcase
Tell Claude Code or Codex "make a promo for my product". The agent captures your real pages, picks shots from a library of tuned motion recipes, storyboards the film, animates it with Remotion , cuts it to the beat, adds sound design, checks every frame and hands you a finished MP4 you can keep editing.
It is not a video generator. Every frame is drawn by code from your own screenshots and copy, so the result is sharp, on-brand and fully editable.
All 216 demos were polished and reviewed. The best versions now make up 124 cards / 150 shots , with fresh Gallery previews and video-shotcraft branding.
2026-09 · Motion Workbench . Keep editing the delivered film in a CapCut-style browser editor.

Built and tuned for Claude Code and Codex. The simplest way is to hand your agent the link:
In mainland China, clone from the AtomGit mirror if GitHub is slow: git clone https://atomgit.com/VincentWei/video-shotcraft.git .
Just describe the film. No command needed.
124 recipe cards in 10 categories, 150 shots in total. Search, filter and copy card names in the Gallery .
Each card lives in references/shots/ / .md , with its Remotion implementation in demos/ / / (see demos/README.md for how to wire one into your project).
After delivery the skill opens a CapCut-style editor in your browser ( node workbench/scripts/open.mjs ). The film is split into shot, transition, caption and SFX tracks exactly as authored. Select any shot to edit its copy, font sizes and colours, move, trim or speed-ramp clips, drag in any of the 150 library shots, then export with Remotion. Preview and render are frame-identical.
Workbench guide, every panel with screenshots (Chinese) · Integration contract
Also in the box: reusable Remotion components (2.5D page camera, captions, flash cuts, digit rolls), Freesound SFX search/download tools and 5 BGM tracks, page-capture scripts, and the production method itself (capture, visual direction, storyboarding, sound design, beat sync, final QA) in references/ .
Share your film. Made something with video-shotcraft? Submit it with the Showcase issue form. After review it appears on the Showcase page .
Remotion downloads its own headless Chrome on first render. Tested on macOS; Linux works with the notes below.
Rendering on a headless Linux box (tested: 2 cores, Node 22) hits three walls:
Concurrency cap. remotion still/render fails with "Maximum for --concurrency is 2" on low-core machines. Pass --concurrency=1 .
Old headless removal. Recent Chrome/Chromium dropped the old headless mode, so pointing Remotion at system Chromium fails to launch. Use a chrome-headless-shell binary instead of full Chrome.
Blocked CDN. If remotion.media is unreachable (common in mainland China), the automatic headless-shell download fails. Pass --browser-executable= .
With these three flags, frame renders from the bundled template work.
For the full workflow see SKILL.md , the production pipeline and the visual QA criteria .
SFX come directly from Freesound , downloaded into each video's project. The shared SFX library has been removed. The sourcing guide covers search, CC0 / CC BY filtering, MP3 preview downloads, measurements and source/credit manifests. The Python CLI uses the standard library; downloading and analysis require FFmpeg. No API key is needed. Sound design covers timing and mixing. The template retains its fixed historical audio for playback and regression checks; new product videos source their SFX from Freesound. BGM options remain in assets/audio/bgm/ .
Product screenshots bundled with the template are demonstration assets. Replace them with screenshots of your product before publishing, and check whether any product, customer or personal data needs to be anonymized.
Freesound audio: each file under its recorded license; retain the project manifest and publish required CC BY credits.
BGM: see ATTRIBUTION.md . Historical template audio: see template credits .
Remotion has its own license : free for individuals and small teams, companies may need a paid license.
Many recipes were distilled by studying the motion language of outstanding official product films, including promos from ClickUp, Perplexity, Slack, Notion, Figma, Framer, Bear, Raycast, Pitch, Miro, Superhuman and Loom . The cards document techniques (timing, easing, choreography) re-implemented from scratch; no footage, artwork or brand assets from these films are included. All trademarks belong to their owners, and none of these companies are affiliated with or endorse this project.
The Freesound sourcing workflow was inspired by vibe-motion/sound . Thanks to its authors for sharing the approach of selecting sounds by source descriptions, duration, download counts, rating counts and licenses. Video Shotcraft's search/download CLI is independently implemented.
Thanks also to Remotion , which powers every demo and template here; Freesound and its contributors for project SFX; Mixkit for BGM and historical template audio; the game-feel and animation communities whose published principles inform several cards; and Claude Code , with which this library was built, iterated and QA'd using the same workflow the skill teaches.
